memos.headline: S09 Parabolic at 52-Week Highs While Most of the Universe Sits in Oversold Downtrends
memos.body: I see a deeply bifurcated tape across this universe as of March 27. S09 is the clear relative-strength leader, sitting at its 52-week high with +41.3% over 12 weeks and +49.0% relative strength vs SPY over the same period, though RSI at 76.1 warns of near-term exhaustion. S07 is the second-best structural story—up +20.4% over 12 weeks, still +28.1% above its 200-day mean, and only -10.3% off highs with RSI at a neutral 46.1, suggesting a healthy consolidation within an uptrend. On the other side, S04 and S02 are in freefall: S04 is -34.2% from its 52-week high with RSI at 22.3 and -25.5% below its 200-day mean, while S02 is an extraordinary -56.8% from its high with persistent negative relative strength. I would avoid catching these falling knives until price reclaims the 50-day mean at minimum; for S04 that means a sustained move above roughly 410, and for S02 above roughly 290.

views.note: At 52-week highs with massive relative strength (+49% vs SPY over 12w), but RSI 76 means I'd trail a stop near 160; a close below 155 would change my view.
Healthy consolidation within a strong uptrend—+28.1% above 200d mean, RSI 46 neutral, only -10.3% off highs; a break below 660 would concern me.
RSI 22.3, -25.5% below 200d mean, -34.2% drawdown with persistent negative relative strength; no sign of a bottom until price reclaims ~410.
Down -56.8% from 52-week high with RSI 30.8 and -17.4% below 200d mean—this is a broken chart and I need to see a close above 290 before reconsidering.
RSI 25.1 is the lowest in the universe, -12.5% below 50d mean with accelerating weekly losses of -8.9%; still above 200d mean (+4.4%) so a hold of ~260 could stabilize, but trend is hostile.
Sitting right at its 200d mean (+0.3%) with RSI 37.9 and modest relative strength vs SPY; a close above 260 (50d area) would turn me constructive.

RSI 30.7 is oversold but 12-week relative strength vs SPY is +6.8%, suggesting underlying resilience; the sharp -14.6% 4-week drop needs to stabilize above 140 or I'd downgrade.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Show Exceptional Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Red on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin compounders and names where earnings power is deteriorating. S10 stands out with 63.1% net margins, 73.2% YoY revenue growth, and 94.5% net income growth on minimal debt ($8.47B), making it the cleanest fundamental story in the group. S04 is similarly compelling at 47.3% net margins with net income up 59.5% YoY, though its $40.26B debt load warrants monitoring. On the other end, S02 is alarming: despite 12.3% revenue growth, net income collapsed 99.8% to essentially zero, implying massive cost or impairment issues that I cannot underwrite. S09 posted revenue contraction of -1.3% alongside a 14.6% decline in net income on a thin 7.9% margin, and S07 grew revenue 18% but saw net income fall 13.9%, suggesting margin headwinds are real. I would need to see operating cash flow and capex detail to gain more conviction on S03 and S08, but their top-line growth and positive earnings trajectories keep them in the constructive camp for now.

views.note: 63.1% net margin, 73% revenue growth, 95% earnings growth, and only $8.47B debt — the strongest fundamental profile in the universe by a wide margin.
47.3% net margin and 59.5% YoY net income growth demonstrate exceptional earnings leverage; would revisit if debt-to-income ratio deteriorates.
30.3% net margin, 18% revenue growth, 29.8% earnings growth, and low debt of $14.79B make this a solid compounder.
$143.76B revenue growing 15.7% with 29.3% net margins is solid, though $88.50B in total debt and lack of segment detail temper my conviction.
Revenue of $213.39B growing 13.6% is impressive scale, but 9.9% net margin and only 5.9% earnings growth suggest limited operating leverage; margin trajectory is the swing factor.
28.4% net margin is healthy but earnings declined 7% YoY and $435.21B in total debt (financial institution) makes the balance sheet opaque without deeper analysis.
19.4% net margin is decent but revenue grew only 1.5% and net income fell 6.7%, suggesting stagnation; need to see if this is cyclical or structural.
Revenue grew 18% but net income fell 13.9% to a 12.5% margin, and $36.21B debt on $19B revenue is heavy leverage — margin compression is the concern.
Revenue contracting 1.3% with net income down 14.6% and a thin 7.9% margin signals deteriorating earnings power; would need a margin inflection to reconsider.
Net income collapsed 99.8% to near zero on $113B revenue despite 12.3% top-line growth — this is a broken earnings story until I see what drove the implosion.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% as Long Rates Back Up and Curve Flattens — Favor Defensives Over Duration
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, while CPI is running at +2.4% y/y — still above target and enough to keep the FOMC patient. Unemployment at 4.40% ticked down 10 bps over three months, signaling a labor market that is softening only gradually, which removes urgency for further easing. The 10y yield has jumped 30 bps over three months to 4.44%, and the 10y-2y spread has compressed 22 bps to +0.46 pp, suggesting the market is repricing for a higher-for-longer rate path and possibly stickier inflation. This backdrop is unfriendly for long-duration growth equities and modestly supportive for banks (positive curve, stable NIM) and staples (defensive in a late-cycle pause). A CPI print breaking above 2.6% y/y or unemployment spiking above 4.6% would change my regime call materially.

views.note: Rising long rates and a pause regime pressure duration-sensitive growth names.
Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve and stable short rates during a pause.
Staples offer defensive positioning as the cycle matures with sticky inflation and a patient Fed.
Cyclicals face mixed signals: labor market is okay but rising yields and a flattening curve suggest caution.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst; stable growth and moderate inflation keep it range-bound.
Higher discount rates from the 30 bps backup in the 10y weigh on high-multiple growth sectors.

memos.headline: S03 and S10 Post-Earnings Negativity May Be Washing Out; S09 Stands Out as Quietly Stable
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K filing cadence and associated price reactions across the universe to gauge sentiment direction. S03 dropped -5.6% on its Feb 5 earnings release and has since filed three additional 8-Ks including a material definitive agreement on Feb 27, suggesting the company is actively managing its narrative—this high filing volume after a sharp selloff can signal a tone inflection if the news is constructive. S10 similarly fell -5.5% on its Feb 25 earnings print and followed up with a leadership change on Mar 6, which adds uncertainty rather than stabilization. S09 posted a muted +0.6% reaction to its Jan 30 earnings and has been quiet since a board change in Feb, which I read as benign sentiment with no negative catalyst building. S05's near-flat -0.5% earnings reaction and subsequent director change are low-signal, while S02's back-to-back officer changes in late Feb/early Mar warrant monitoring for governance noise.

views.note: Heavy post-selloff filing activity including a material agreement hints at narrative repair after the -5.6% earnings drop; tone may be turning.
The -5.5% earnings reaction followed by a leadership departure signals unresolved negative sentiment with no clear stabilization yet.
Muted +0.6% earnings reaction and quiet filing cadence since suggest stable-to-positive sentiment baseline with no crowding.
Near-flat earnings reaction and routine filings provide no directional sentiment signal; director change is low-impact.
Two officer-change filings in quick succession plus an FD disclosure create mild governance noise but no clear negative or positive tone shift.
Single 'Other Events' 8-K filed just yesterday provides insufficient signal to form a directional view.

memos.headline: Surging Oil and Policy Uncertainty Signal Escalating Geopolitical Risk Across the Universe
memos.body: I am seeing a dramatic deterioration in the geopolitical risk backdrop: WTI crude has surged 70% over three months to $96.18/bbl, the VIX has doubled over the same period to 27.44, and the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index sits at an elevated 509.77 (+60% month-over-month). The flattening yield curve (10y-2y spread down 22bp over 3 months to 0.46pp) and widening HY spreads (+35bp over 3 months to 3.21%) confirm that markets are pricing in both growth risk and policy-driven disruption—consistent with sanctions escalation, energy supply dislocation, or new export controls rather than a garden-variety slowdown. I lack granular GDELT event data to pinpoint the exact catalyst, but the oil move's magnitude and speed strongly suggest a structural supply-side shock, likely tied to Middle East or Russia-related sanctions enforcement. Multiple 8-K filings across S03, S06, S07, and S02 in recent weeks hint at material disclosures that may relate to supply-chain or regulatory adjustments. My conviction is highest on energy-exposed names and lowest on companies with opaque China/sanctions exposure until we get more detail; a de-escalation in oil above $90 or a rollback of any new sanctions would change my view.

views.note: Three 8-K filings in three weeks suggest active disclosure of material events, possibly sanctions or supply-chain related, but without detail I cannot take a directional view.
Two 8-K filings including a Reg FD disclosure in February may reflect preemptive positioning around policy shifts, but elevated uncertainty warrants caution rather than conviction.

A fresh 8-K on March 26 amid a VIX at 27.44 and oil near $96 raises the risk that this name is exposed to the geopolitical shock driving markets; I would stay away until the filing content is clarified.
March 9 Reg FD disclosure is too opaque to act on, but the macro backdrop of surging oil and policy uncertainty argues against adding risk here.
January Reg FD filing is stale relative to the March oil and volatility spike; I have no evidence of direct geopolitical exposure but the macro environment keeps me sidelined.
With HY spreads widening 35bp over three months and policy uncertainty near 510, any name lacking clear defensive positioning is vulnerable; the February 8-K offers no reassurance.
